misconception_description: Student believes that it is unnecessary for loop variables to be explicitly initialized before the loop.

solutions.generated_code:
program CariTerkecil
kamus
  n, i, x, terkecil : integer
algoritma
  input(n)
  i <- 0
  for i <- 1 to n do
    input(x)
    if i == 1 then
      terkecil <- x
    else
      if x < terkecil then
        terkecil <- x
      endif
    endif
  endfor
  output(terkecil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student unnecessarily initializes the loop variable 'x' before the for loop, believing this is required. In reality, the for loop automatically creates and manages the loop variable. The initialization to 0 is immediately overwritten when the loop begins iterating through list1, so while unnecessary, it doesn't affect the correctness of the code. The student believes this initialization is proper practice and doesn't realize the for loop handles variable creation automatically.
